items.sentence: That is why I will fight for better health, better homes, good education and decent jobs, and fight to tackle the biggest crises we face: the cost of living and the climate crisis.
I committed during the campaign to using my seat in this House to pressure the Government to take serious action on the issue of sewage, and I promise to do so.

I will continue to work with the sector to understand its concerns, and to listen to patients, and I will ensure that the contract reforms we have introduced this year are just the start of building an NHS dental system of which we can all be proud.
I will continue to campaign alongside local residents to ensure that access to NHS care is quick and easily available to everybody who needs it.

Securing the return of the family doctor is a popular and much-needed policy locally, and I mean to ensure that we deliver it, just as I will continue to campaign for the delivery of our much-needed new hospital.

I commit to continuing that important work, and welcome the moves being made by this Government to rebuild our transport services to be run for the people, benefiting our economy, opportunity and the environment.
The NHS gave me a second chance at life, and so as Health Secretary I will fight for the NHS every day with the strength it has given me back.

While I remain committed to ensuring that any Bill put forward is robust so that we do not have to fix problems in primary legislation, as we had to in the case of the 2024 Act, I am seized of the urgency of both presenting the Bill and commencing the ground rent provisions as quickly as possible.
I will work to ensure that our justice system prioritises victims’ rights, tackles delays and restores public confidence.
I will fight for every LGBT veteran to get the compensation that they deserve.

I will continue to fight for every one of those young people and for their loving but often terrified families to get the care they need through mental health services, but why can we not choose to do something radical today that will reduce the number of people suffering mental ill health in the first place?

I want my constituents who are watching, feeling let down and having been left out of pocket by unacceptable conduct, to know that as their MP I will continue to fight on their behalf and alongside them for justice.
In my last career, prior to entering this House, I was incredibly proud to represent our NHS and other healthcare providers, and I will continue to fight for our NHS now that I sit here as an MP.
The Defence Secretary and I remain committed to driving this work forward until every recommendation of Lord Etherton’s review is implemented.
I remain committed to helping and assisting victims, to ensure that they get the justice and support they deserve.
I remain committed to the indicative timetable that was published in July, which will see elections to new councils in May 2027 and those new councils going live in April 2028, subject to Parliament.
I am honoured to serve, and I pledge to work across party lines to ensure economic security and improvements in our public services—and I will do so in a friendly, open and approachable way.

With the Labour Campaign for International Development, and now as a member of the International Development Committee, I remain committed to taking forward her legacy, particularly on the responsibility to protect civilians, which is so urgent everywhere from Ukraine to Syria to Sudan.
I remain committed to strengthening trade union rights across the board.
I will defend our local hospital, and I will campaign on primary care, too.

I will defend the decisions taken by this Government to help working people, grow the economy and fix the mess we inherited from the previous Government, and we are doing so with fairer tax at the core.

I join colleagues in remembering the 72 people who lost their lives in the Grenfell Tower fire tragedy, and I say to their friends and families that I will always fight to deliver justice for their loved ones.

In this Session, I will vote against inhumane, unjust and unfair policies wherever they appear; defend our public services and the funding they need to thrive; and give voice to my constituents of every faith or none and of every colour and creed who refuse to look away from injustice abroad.

I will defend to my death the right of people to disagree with me, to hold different opinions about the future of this country and to resolve those through the democratic process, but I will not let myself be silenced or sidelined by them.
I pledge to work tirelessly with my good friends in the co-operative movement, the trade unions and this House to give retail workers the dignity and protection at work that they need.

I am committed to ensuring that workers are able to enforce their employment rights, and we are working closely with the Ministry of Justice to ensure that happens, looking into what further improvements we can make to the way in which ACAS and employment tribunals operate.
I am calling for mandatory training for social care staff, in line with the dementia training standards framework, which is absolutely essential, and I will continue to campaign for that.
We will consult on a new victims code shortly, and I am determined to ensure that we get that new code right for all victims, including the children of those heinous criminals.
I will always defend farms, the rural economy and our rural areas during my time in the House.

Our farmers face numerous challenges, from the impact of rural crime to the effects of climate change on crops and livestock, and I am committed to advocating for farmers’ needs and supporting sustainable practices.
These are enormous challenges, which is why I am determined to ensure that every penny that goes into the health service is well spent.
It is crucial that investment in vital services and local infrastructure keeps pace with development, and that is something that I will champion in my constituency.

The greatest-ever expansion of community energy projects, delivering a million new owners of energy, will be genuinely transformational, and as a proud Co-operative party MP, I will champion the growth of such projects, so that local people will benefit from our green transition too.
Tackling sexual violence against women and the abuse of women and promoting the safety of women and children are things I will champion, not deny.
As a Back Bencher, I will always fight for more funding to modernise our steel industry.

Tragically, we lost Paul within days of my election, so he is not here with us today, but I will continue to fight to break down all the barriers to opportunity that our children and young people face.
Food banks and the alleviation of poverty in the UK are very important personally to me, and I will champion them strongly during my time in Parliament.

With all eyes on the middle east, this House expects, and I am determined to ensure, that we will continue to confront the growing threats in the High North, to fulfil our obligations to NATO and to step up support for Ukraine.
I am determined to ensure that the rights, voices and spaces for women who work in the NHS and women who are patients in the NHS are protected.
In this place, I will always stand up for small businesses and the self-employed.

As a delegate to the Council of Europe, I will always defend the European convention on human rights and its institution and treaties, and that is why it is important to talk about it in the correct context.

Because I am determined to ensure that the energy technologies of the future are built here and owned here and that jobs come to Britain, this spending review invests in the wholly publicly owned Great British Energy, headquartered in Scotland.
I am determined to ensure that we build the transport infrastructure needed to drive economic growth and opportunity in every part of the country, including the rural north.
I will champion our local farmers so that we can boost food security and sustain the rural economy that forms an important part of my constituency.
I will oppose any measures by this Government, including the misguided nationalisation of industry and the socialist labour rules, that I believe will hamper or reverse that trend.
I will always campaign for electoral reform so that everybody’s vote really counts.
It is also why I am determined to ensure that British businesses are invested in and grow in the UK so that we have the supply of critical minerals that we need.
Secondly, I will focus on education for our children, and I will fight to ensure that all children, whatever their background and circumstances, get the opportunities that they deserve in life.
That is why I will always champion my constituents’ right to good-quality, genuinely affordable homes.

In conclusion, I promise to work tirelessly for my constituents, not only on fixing our railways, but on other issues too, such as the fact that our schools are among the lowest funded in the country and that it is almost impossible to register with an NHS dentist locally.
I will continue to advocate in this place for truth, justice and lasting change, and for Grenfell bereaved and survivors to be heard.

We are rebuilding the relationship, and I will continue to advocate that my colleagues in Government do that at pace, with urgency, and with increasing ambition, because it is so fundamental to all our growth prospects for the future.
I will continue to advocate for transparency so that victims can understand how sentencing works.
In this role, I am committed to supporting all people across Northern Ireland.
I am committed to supporting our farmers and our fishing industry—the lifeblood of our community.
I am determined to see the walk-in centre reopened at St Mark’s hospital after it was closed down as a temporary measure at the beginning of covid lockdown.

I fear the new Government’s top-down housing targets will further compound that issue, and I will do all I can to ensure that the right mix of houses are built, in the right places, with the right infrastructure and public consultation.
We must do much, much better in Scotland for the survivors of domestic abuse, and I am determined to continue to work hard on this.

I understand entirely, and I will always champion those who served in Northern Ireland, whether in the Royal Irish Regiment most recently, in the Home Service Battalions until their disbandment in 2007, or indeed in the Ulster Defence Regiment.
As a biased former care worker, I will always champion carers and the complex quality and professional work that they do.
I am determined to see more trafficking offenders brought to justice.

Following 15 years working overseas, I am committed to contributing to the resetting of our standing in the world, recognising our international obligations and participating fully in our international institutions, which will include restoring a closer relationship with our closest neighbour, Europe.
I will always champion public services, and I will stand up for investment so that local people benefit.
I am determined to see a defence dividend of investment in British jobs and apprentices, including in his constituency.
I will always fight for farmers, to improve farming incomes and to support farming communities.

Devolution is massively important to me—I knocked on doors to campaign for the creation of the Scottish Parliament—and I will defend it with my life, but we want to ensure that it works for everyone, so that there is no chance of “big boy done it and ran away.”
That is why I will not rest until we have completed our health mission to restore the fundamental promise of our NHS: that it will be there for all our constituents when they need it.

I am committed to improving our transport links, which currently hamper growth and divide communities, and to securing better access to healthcare services and provision for special educational needs and disabilities in the constituency.
I am committed to improving local mental health services to help young people build the resilience they need to live happy and healthy lives.
Social and environmental justice are part of the same struggle, and I will not stop fighting until we deliver both for the British people.
There will be thousands of contracts in the supply chain, with huge opportunities for Northern Ireland, and I am determined to deliver them.

As a carer myself for much of my life, I am determined to speak up for the millions of carers less fortunate than I am—the millions of family carers and care workers who make enormous sacrifices looking after loved ones, the carers who keep our NHS going and the carers who keep our society going.
I look forward to continuing this campaign with all of you, and I promise that I will not stop until injured emergency service workers get the recognition they deserve.

Although it is important that in the immediate aftermath of the attack we consider security matters, enhancing the police presence and deepening our work with the Community Security Trust, I will not stop until people in this country can go to a synagogue or Jewish school without first having to go through a security cordon.
Their advocacy inspires me in my role here, and I will continue fighting alongside them for a compassionate, just and workable asylum system.

I will continue to campaign for good access to NHS dentists across my community for as long as it takes, and I am glad to finally have a Government who I can work with—rather than have to fight against—to get the NHS dental services we need locally.
I will continue to campaign for that hospital until the day it is built.

On behalf of so many families in my constituency, I will continue to campaign for the right to food to be enshrined in UK law, so that everyone is legally protected from the scourge of hunger and we can end the obscene growth of food banks since 2010, which was caused by political choices.
As an academic lawyer, I will do all I can to defend the rule of law, which is under threat from our badly neglected and crumbling civil and criminal justice system.
Although the NHS in Wales faces many challenges and competing demands for future investment, I will continue to press the new Welsh Government to participate in the ISE.
I will be a strong voice for Scotland at Westminster.
As your MP I will work closely with the Chief Constable to tackle key areas, including county lines drug dealing in our towns, antisocial behaviour, rural crime and domestic violence.

It takes guts and a huge leap of faith to go into business, and so I’m committed to giving them the best chance to thrive through cuts to business rates, making sure invoices get paid on time, and pushing to make Britain the high-growth, start-up hub of the world.
I will work to protect and enhance our health services, improve access and reduce waiting times.
I will always support measures to make our high streets and communities safer for all workers.

As your MP I will champion council housing as I have always done, use my experience as a Council Cabinet Member to hold the police to account and tackle crime in the constituency, and offer a new model of politics for the area, putting the community at its heart.
I will continue to press the Government for fair treatment of the workers our care system depends on.
And, throughout this collaboration, I will campaign to build momentum and generate cross-party support for financial education reforms.
As MP I will work to bring central government jobs to our city, and support the further expansion of low carbon technologies across our region.
I will continue campaigning to get our local NHS back on its feet and fit for the future, so that local residents can rely on getting first class care when they need it.

The Labour Government has set out a range of crucial measures to reduce violence against women and girls, preventing youth crime and to rebuild our criminal justice system which I will always support in Parliament.

I will continue to press for stronger protections, including an independent children's online safety advocate as called for by the NSPCC, and for proper digital literacy education so children and parents are equipped to navigate the online world safely.
Off the back of these recommendations I will be therefore be launching a campaign for a ‘Community Health Hub’ for South Dereham.
As your MP I will fully support Hinchingbrooke's plans to build a brand new hospital and will campaign to secure the funding needed for the redevelopment of the site.
I will continue the fight for a new clinical unit at Wycombe Hospital to replace the ageing tower, as well as more GP surgeries, such as at Long Crendon.
As an MP, I will work tirelessly to make sure that our environment is protected, particularly by ending the pumping of raw sewage into our waterways.
I will continue meeting with pharmacists, local NHS representatives, and GPs to discuss how these initiatives are progressing and where the new government can support local services effectively.
As your MP, I will Champion an industrial strategy that delivers investment in renewable energy sources like solar, wind and biomass, so that we keep energy bills low for good.
As your MP, I will Campaign for a comprehensive NHS workforce plan that ensures we have enough GPs, nurses, midwives and dentists to serve our local communities.
As your MP, I will Campaign for a fair school funding settlement which enables children in every corner of the constituency to attend a good local school regardless of postcode.
As your MP, I will Fight to make permanent the £2 bus fare cap that connects Buckingham with Milton Keynes, Aylesbury, Oxford and Bedford.
Locally I want to ensure that houses have sufficient insulation and I will be supporting the development of Great British Energy.
I will present the Bill to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero, urging its adoption.

I have pledged to do everything possible to secure more money for our local schools. One of the most significant barriers to learning that has become more prominent over the last decade is poor mental health.
I will push firmly for this issue to be addressed in Parliament and have prioritised ensuring that the young people in our community have access to specialist mental health hubs.
I will continue to push for massive reform of this totally failing sector to ensure that carers, and those they care for, get the support they need.
